title: Verde Buenas ampalaya (Verde Buenas F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Verde Buenas ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety from Ramgo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Verde Buenas ampalaya is an F1 hybrid ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Verde Buenas F1. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Verde Buenas ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Verde Buenas F1, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 30 to 40 days after transplanting.
**Yield:** 20 to 25 t/ha potential (company figure), with picking lasting up to two months.
**Fruit:** Cylindrical, shiny light green with smooth ridges, 30 to 35 cm long and 4 to 5 cm across.
Tolerant to the 'namamarako' virus and to fine cracks on the fruit.
Does best in the cool season and the hot wet season.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: showcased by Ramgo as its answer to fruit cracking and 'pamamarako' and still in Ramgo's professional bitter gourd line. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual ampalaya on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Verde Buenas ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Verde Buenas F1 the same as Verde Buenas?
items.a: Yes. Verde Buenas F1 is another name for Verde Buenas. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Verde Buenas?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
